blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Global logistics strategy, at senior level, is about deciding consciously which regions the company will treat as strategic anchors, which as secondary markets, and which as merely opportunistic. Those three categories demand different governance, different investment, and different tolerance for disruption. Treating them all alike is the classic mistake — it spreads attention and resources thin, and it leaves the anchors under-supported precisely when they need real help.

The useful frame at this level is not lowest cost. It is the balance of cost, service, resilience, and access across a changing world. A dependence on one region for critical lanes is cheap until the political weather changes. A diversified footprint is more expensive until a single region becomes unusable. The right answer depends on the company's strategic tolerance for surprise.

Had we diversified our European base two years ago, the last disruption would have been a bad week instead of a bad quarter. These are the questions senior leaders are paid to answer before the disruption begins — not during it.

items.q: According to the text, what is the "classic mistake" in global logistics?
items.why: "Treating them all alike is the classic mistake" — as três categorias exigem tratamentos diferentes.

items.q: How does the text describe the trade-off between concentration and diversification?
options: Concentration is cheap until the political weather changes; a diversified footprint is dearer until a region becomes unusable
Diversification is cheap until a crisis hits
Both cost roughly the same over time
Concentration is always the safer choice
items.why: O texto contrasta os dois: dependência de uma região é barata até o clima político mudar; a pegada diversificada custa mais até uma região ficar inutilizável.

items.q: The phrase "the right answer depends on the company's strategic tolerance for surprise" suggests that…
options: there is no single correct logistics design for every company
cost is the only real variable
items.why: Inferência: se a resposta depende da tolerância de cada empresa, então não existe um desenho único e universalmente correto.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Lowest cost is the right organising principle for global logistics
Regional categories should carry different governance
Resilience has a real, if delayed, payoff
Strategic anchors deserve stronger support than opportunistic markets
items.why: Inferência: o texto afirma explicitamente que "the useful frame is not lowest cost" — o autor discordaria dessa premissa.

items.q: The final example ("Had we diversified… a bad week instead of a bad quarter") is used mainly to…
options: illustrate the cost of not deciding before a disruption
show that diversification is always cheaper
items.why: Inferência: o exemplo hipotético mostra o preço de não ter respondido a essas perguntas antes da disrupção, reforçando o ponto final do texto.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James abrindo a revisão de estratégia logística global. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thank you all for making the time. I want to be candid about why we are in this room. Last quarter, a regional disruption cost us most of a quarter of margin — and, more worrying, it exposed a dependence the board did not know we had.

Here is what I keep coming back to. Had we diversified our European lanes eighteen months ago, that event would have been a bad week, not a bad quarter. We didn't, because diversification looked expensive and the concentrated route looked cheap. On paper it was cheap — right up until the political weather turned.

So I am not asking you to cut cost this morning. I am asking us to be honest about which regions are genuine strategic anchors and which we are treating as anchors only out of habit. The anchors get real investment and real resilience. The secondary markets get a lighter touch. The opportunistic ones get governance before they get capital.

What I will not accept is another review that ends with a spreadsheet and no decision. We answer these questions now, calmly — or we answer them again in the middle of the next disruption, and far less calmly.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why did James call this review?
options: The board asked him to cut logistics costs
A regional disruption cost most of a quarter and revealed a hidden dependence
A competitor entered the European market
A new supplier failed an audit
items.why: "a regional disruption cost us the better part of three months of margin… it exposed a dependence the board did not know we had."

items.q: Why did the company originally choose the concentrated route?
options: Diversification looked expensive and concentration looked cheap
It was faster to set up
items.why: "diversification looked expensive and the concentrated route looked cheap."

items.q: What does James say he is NOT asking for this morning?
items.why: "I am not asking you to cut cost this morning."

items.q: What does James imply about some of the current "anchor" regions?
options: They are only anchors out of habit, not genuine strategy
They are the cheapest to operate
items.why: Inferência: ele pede honestidade sobre "which we are treating as anchors only out of habit", sugerindo que alguns não são âncoras reais.

items.q: What is James's underlying warning in his closing lines?
options: The next review should produce a detailed spreadsheet
The team should postpone the decision indefinitely
If they don't decide calmly now, they will decide badly during the next crisis
items.why: Inferência: "we answer these questions now, calmly — or we answer them again in the middle of the next disruption, and far less calmly."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Germany is a strategic anchor for us; we build the whole network around it." A strategic anchor is…
options: a region entered only for quick gains
a core region the strategy is built around
items.why: Strategic anchor = âncora estratégica: a região central em torno da qual a estratégia se organiza.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "That region for us is purely ___ — we're there while the margins last, nothing more."
items.why: Opportunistic = oportunista: presença mantida apenas enquanto compensa, sem compromisso estrutural.

items.q: "The route from Rotterdam to Singapore is a critical lane." A critical lane is…
options: a transport route the business cannot afford to lose
a secondary market with low volume
items.why: Critical lane = rota crítica: um corredor logístico do qual o negócio depende e não pode perder.

items.q: Choose the correct phrase: "A ___ absorbs shocks better than relying on a single region."
items.why: Diversified footprint = pegada diversificada: presença distribuída que amortece choques melhor que a concentração.

items.q: "Cheap until the political weather changes." Political weather here means…
options: actual climate conditions along the route
the shifting political and geopolitical conditions of a region
items.why: Political weather = clima político: as condições geopolíticas mutáveis que podem inviabilizar uma rota.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em revisões de estratégia logística. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the diversification plan." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the new routing model region by region." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva, por etapas.

items.q: "Two regional heads pushed back on cutting the secondary markets." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "Building resilience now should pay off the next time a region goes dark." To pay off means to…
items.why: Pay off = compensar, gerar um retorno que valeu o investimento — aqui, a resiliência recompensa numa disrupção futura.

items.q: "A tidy spreadsheet won't move the needle on our exposure." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível — aqui, não muda a exposição real ao risco.
